subject: Customer keys, operator visibility limits, and cross-border evidence request
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma.legal@healthsync.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: David Chen <david.chen@healthsync.io>, HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.io>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 23:05:00 +0000
Subject: Clarification on BYOK scope, operator access, and EU transfers

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo today — helpful. Before we move to contracting, our security and legal teams need clarity on a few privacy points for a private VPC/on-prem deployment where we will manage customer keys (BYOK):

- Who holds the KMS root/CMK? For our use case we plan to maintain the CMK. We need to confirm whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext or any key material.
- What operator activities would require the operator (Redwood ops) to access customer data or the keystore? Please enumerate conditions and escalation paths.
- We must document subprocessors involved in the private deployment (monitoring, logging collectors, patch management) and the locations where those services run.
- If we route inference traffic through EU-only zones but require emergency failover to US-based capacity, what controls/logs do you provide to demonstrate no substantive data transfer occurred, and what contractual safeguards do you propose?

Can you send a short, itemized response and any evidence pack you can share (audit logs, attestation, and a minimal operator access matrix)? We need this for our DPA negotiation team.

Best,
Emma Park
Senior Counsel, HealthSync

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma.legal@healthsync.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on BYOK scope, operator access, and EU transfers

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers inline below; attaching a concise operator matrix and an evidence checklist. Happy to hop on a short call with your security leads.

- CMK custody: Customer holds the CMK. Redwood can be configured for customer-managed keys where the CMK never leaves the customer KMS. We do not store raw key material. (See attachment: redwood-operator-access-matrix.pdf)
- Operator access triggers: Routine ops do NOT have key material access. Escalations that may require operator intervention are limited to (a) node forensics after a suspected host compromise, (b) break-glass for cluster recovery if customer consents or a previously agreed emergency procedure is invoked. For both cases we provide recorded jump-host sessions and require two-person authorization.
- Subprocessors: For private VPCs we limit subprocessors to kernel/hypervisor vendors and a managed-patching partner; logging aggregation is customer-deployed or run in a customer-owned logging VPC. We will supply the subprocessor roster and regions in the DPA annex.
- Cross-border failover: We support region affinity and prefer EU-only routing. For emergency failover to US regions, we provide live transfer logs, a transfer reason, and a signed attestation with timestamps. We can commit to a contractual clause requiring notification and a limit on the data types that may be routed during failover.

Next steps: I asked Irene (security) to add technical specifics and the sample clause language for your legal team. Laura, can you prepare the DPA annex language for an EU-residency exception/failover carve-out?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-operator-access-matrix.pdf, evidence-request-checklist.xlsx

-----
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma.legal@healthsync.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on BYOK scope, operator access, and EU transfers

Emma — adding a few technical guardrails to make this actionable for your ops/security reviewers: see inline bullets.

- BYOK mode: When configured for customer KMS, Redwood services run with an agent that requests ephemeral data keys (DEKs) from the customer CMK via a signed request. The DEK is held only in encrypted process memory and is zeroed after the inference session. We log all DEK issuance calls to a tamper-evident ledger (hash-chained logs).
- No plaintext keys: Redwood will never hold plaintext CMK or persistent DEKs; only ephemeral DEKs in RAM for active sessions. We can provide a memory-zeroing proof checklist from our runtime team and ephemeral key TTL defaults.
- Operator access matrix: Operators can access (1) host metrics and kernel traces, (2) sanitized request metadata (token counts, latency), (3) encrypted model artifacts. Operators cannot decrypt model inputs/outputs without the DEK. For break-glass recovery we require: customer approval OR invocation of the emergency DPA clause, two ops signatures, recorded session, and a post-incident report delivered within 48 hours.
- Audit evidence we can provide immediately: DEK issuance logs (redacted), jump-host session recordings for past month (redacted), SOC2+ controls mapping, and a signed statement on subprocessor list. We cannot provide raw customer payloads.

If HealthSync wants, we can prepare a 1-page technical appendix describing the DEK flow + log samples for legal review.

—Irene
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Emma Park <emma.legal@healthsync.io>

Subject: Re: Clarification on BYOK scope, operator access, and EU transfers

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of follow-ups before we move the DPA redline: 

1) Can you produce a one-page DEK flow diagram plus a 7-day sample of DEK issuance logs (redacted) and a sample jump-host recording to kick off our review?
2) For the contractual carve-out on emergency failover, we want a clause that: (a) requires 24-hour notice when feasible, (b) limits the types of payloads that may be routed in failover, and (c) guarantees deletion of routed copies within 7 days unless legal hold is invoked.

If you can provide the materials by Monday EOD (HealthSync legal timetable), we will circulate an initial redline.

Regards,
Emma

-----
